quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 2011 Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 2011 paper, spanning calculus, matrices, vectors, probability, integrals, differential equations and LPP. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If y = log(sin x), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: Differentiate the log: dy/dx = (1/sin x) · cos x = cot x.

questions.q: If A is a square matrix with det(A) = 3, then det(A<sup>−1</sup>) equals:
Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of 1/(1 + x<sup>2</sup>) dx.
questions.explanation: The antiderivative is tan<sup>−1</sup> x, so the value is tan<sup>−1</sup>(1) − tan<sup>−1</sup>(0) = π/4.

questions.q: The integrating factor of the differential equation dy/dx + y = e<sup>x</sup> is:
questions.explanation: For dy/dx + Py = Q the integrating factor is e<sup>∫P dx</sup>. Here P = 1, so IF = e<sup>x</sup>.

questions.q: If P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2, then P(A ∪ B) equals:
questions.explanation: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B) = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7.

questions.q: The value of the scalar triple product i · (j × k) is:
questions.explanation: j × k = i, and i · i = 1, so the scalar triple product equals 1.

questions.q: In a linear programming problem, the optimal value of the objective function occurs at:
options: the centre of the feasible region
a corner (vertex) of the feasible region
questions.explanation: By the corner-point theorem, an optimal value of a linear objective over a bounded feasible region is attained at a vertex.

questions.q: If a matrix A is both symmetric and skew-symmetric, then A is:
questions.explanation: Symmetric means A<sup>T</sup> = A and skew-symmetric means A<sup>T</sup> = −A, so A = −A, which forces A to be the zero matrix.

faq.q: How hard was the CBSE Class 12 Mathematics 2011 paper?
faq.a: The 2011 paper followed the standard board pattern of that era, with a spread of short-answer and long-answer questions across calculus, algebra, vectors and probability. Most questions were direct applications of NCERT concepts, so students who had worked through the textbook found it fair.

faq.q: Which chapters carried the most weight in the 2011 paper?
faq.a: Calculus dominated, as it usually does in Class 12 — continuity and differentiability, applications of derivatives, and integration together carried the largest share of marks. Matrices, determinants, vectors, three-dimensional geometry, probability and linear programming filled out the rest.

faq.q: Is it still worth solving a 2011 paper today?
faq.a: Yes. The syllabus for topics like integrals, differential equations and vectors has stayed broadly stable, so an older paper is good drill for accuracy and speed. Just check the current CBSE blueprint for the exact marking scheme and any dropped topics before you rely on it for weightage.

faq.q: How should I use a past paper for revision?
faq.a: Solve it in one timed sitting without notes, then mark it honestly against the answers. Note every question you got wrong, revisit that concept in your textbook, and re-attempt similar questions a few days later so the correction actually sticks.
